mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median realized return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.5% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically distinguishable from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which compresses earnings and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 2% over two months signals a deflationary monetary easing, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls AND CPIAUCSL < 2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the realized return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE (unemployment rate) over two months signals a labor market normalization after a deep recession, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE rises above 4% in two consecutive months after a prior period of both falling
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly positive at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer spending, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered months, or the average return is not significantly positive at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in Real Personal Income (proxied by RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates expanding household purchasing power, which supports consumer demand and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive in at least 70% of triggered periods, or the median return is not distinguishable from zero at 5% significance.
